title: Lattice dimension and freeness from regularity at a toric vertex
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $R$ a fine saturated sharp commutative monoid whose group completion is torsion free, of rank $r$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Let $A$ be the set of nonzero elements not expressible as a sum of two nonzero elements, and assume that $A$ is finite and generates $R$. Fix a finite $t\geq0$ and put $B=k[R][y_1^{\pm1},\ldots,y_t^{\pm1}]$, $\mathfrak m=(e^q:q\ne0)+(y_j-1:1\leq j\leq t)$ [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Assume that the cotangent space $\mathfrak m B_{\mathfrak m}/(\mathfrak m B_{\mathfrak m})^2$ has $k$-dimension $|A|+t$, using $B/\mathfrak m=k$. Then $B$ is a finite type integral domain [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], its fraction field is a rational function field in $r+t$ variables over $k$, and
$$\dim B_{\mathfrak m}=r+t$$
for Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. If $B_{\mathfrak m}$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], then $|A|=r$, the images of the atoms form a $\mathbf Z$-basis of $R^{\rm gp}$, and the homomorphism $\mathbf N^A\to R$, $(n_a)\mapsto\sum_a n_a a$, is an isomorphism. Empty sets and rank zero are allowed.

source.place: VIII proof of Lemma 3.2.12(ii), pp.104--105: dimension versus cotangent dimension, then independence of the atom generators; rational-function-field and integer-matrix arguments expanded by an agent.

proof.text: Put $G=R^{\rm gp}$, $H=G\oplus\mathbf Z^t$ and $Q=R\oplus\mathbf Z^t\subset H$. The injection follows from integrality in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. The finite set consisting of $(a,0)$ for $a\in A$ and $(0,\pm e_j)$ generates $Q$ as a monoid; it generates $H$ as a group because $A$ generates $R$. Sending the monomial indexed by $(q,(n_j))$ to $e^q\prod_j y_j^{n_j}$ identifies $k[Q]$ with $B$: it is a bijection of their monomial bases and respects multiplication, by [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. In particular $B$ is generated as a $k$-algebra by the finite family $e^a,y_j,y_j^{-1}$, so is finite type by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: VIII, proof of Lemma 3.2.12(ii), p.104: finite monoid generators and the inclusion in the group algebra; explicit product-monoid version.

proof.text: The group $G$ is finitely generated by the images of $A$ and is torsion free by hypothesis. By [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] it has an integral basis, of size $r$ by the stipulated rank. Adjoining the $t$ standard basis vectors gives a basis $h_1,\ldots,h_{r+t}$ of $H$. The group $H$ is torsion free, so [lem-trf-monoid-algebra-domain-fraction], applied to $Q\subset H$ with the finite generation and group generation checked in Step 1, shows that $B$ is a domain and identifies its fraction field with that of $k[H]$. The first clause of [lem-trf-lattice-torus-coordinates-action] identifies $k[H]$ with $k[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_{r+t}^{\pm1}]$, by $e^{\sum n_i h_i}\mapsto\prod z_i^{n_i}$.

source.place: VIII, Lemma 3.2.12(ii), p.104, k[P] contained in k[Pgp] isomorphic to k[Z^n]; lattice coordinates as in 3.2.4.

proof.text: Write $n=r+t$. The fraction field of $k[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_n^{\pm1}]$ is $k(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$: a Laurent polynomial is an ordinary polynomial divided by a monomial, so a quotient of Laurent polynomials is a quotient of ordinary polynomials, and the reverse inclusion is immediate. The variables are algebraically independent because distinct polynomial monomials remain distinct basis elements in the Laurent ring, hence in its fraction field. Every rational function $f=P(z)/Q(z)$, with $Q\ne0$, satisfies $Q(z)f-P(z)=0$, a nonzero polynomial relation in an extra indeterminate. Thus no element outside the displayed variables can be adjoined to them algebraically independently. They form a transcendence basis; [def-kun-transcendence-degree] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\operatorname{Frac}(B)=n$. For $n=0$ the Laurent ring and its fraction field are $k$, and the same argument uses the empty transcendence basis.

source.place: Tags 030E (definition-transcendence) and 030G (definition-transcendence-degree): explicit monomial calculation of the rational-function-field basis.

proof.text:
There is a $k$-algebra map $\epsilon:B	o k$ sending $e^0$ to $1$, every $e^q$ with $q
e0$ to $0$, and every $y_j$ to $1$. It respects multiplication: sharpness says that a sum of two monoid elements can be zero only when both are zero. Its kernel is exactly the specified $\mathfrak m$. Indeed, modulo the nonzero monomials any element is a Laurent polynomial in the $y_j$, and a Laurent polynomial minus its value at $(1,\ldots,1)$ belongs to $(y_j-1)_j$ by telescoping products and the identities $y^d-1=(y-1)(1+\cdots+y^{d-1})$, $y^{-d}-1=-y^{-d}(y^d-1)$ for $d>0$. Thus $B/\mathfrak m=k$ and $\mathfrak m$ is maximal. The residue map on $B_{\mathfrak m}$ is $b/s\mapsto\epsilon(b)/\epsilon(s)$; it is onto with kernel $\mathfrak m B_{\mathfrak m}$, since $s
otin\mathfrak m$ means $\epsilon(s)
e0$. This fixes the residue-field identification used in the cotangent hypothesis.

source.place: VIII, Lemma 3.2.12(ii), pp.104--105: monomial maximal ideal with residue field k; Laurent variables evaluated at one.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] to the finite type $k$-domain $B$ from Steps 1--2 and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ from Step 4. Its statement gives $\dim B_{\mathfrak m}=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\operatorname{Frac}(B)$, not merely the topological dimension at an arbitrary point. Step 3 computes the right hand side as $r+t$. This proves the claimed Krull dimension without any regularity assumption.

source.place: Tag 00P0, lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring: finite type domain dimension equals function-field transcendence degree, including every maximal localization.

proof.text: Now assume $C=B_{\mathfrak m}$ is regular local. It is a Noetherian local ring by [def-weil-regular-scheme], with residue field $k$ by Step 4. The regularity equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] gives $\dim_k(\mathfrak m C/(\mathfrak m C)^2)=\dim C$. The assumed cotangent dimension and Step 5 therefore give $|A|+t=r+t$. Cancelling the finite natural number $t$ yields $|A|=r$.

source.place: Tag 00KU, definition-regular-local and preceding cotangent-dimension discussion; applied to ILO VIII Lemma 3.2.12(ii), pp.104--105.

proof.text: Let $\phi:\mathbf Z^A\to G$ send the standard vector indexed by $a$ to its image in $G$. It is onto because $A$ generates $R$ and every element of $G$ is a difference of elements of $R$. The basis of $G$ in Step 2 and $|A|=r$ give an isomorphism $\theta:G\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf Z^A$ by choosing a bijection of their finite basis index sets. Hence $\phi\theta$ is a surjective $\mathbf Z$-linear endomorphism of the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-module $G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-surjective-endomorphism-bijective] it is an isomorphism. Since $\theta$ is an isomorphism, $\phi$ is an isomorphism as well. By the basis convention of [def-weil-pbc-free-module], the images of the atoms form a $\mathbf Z$-basis of $G$.

source.place: Tag 05G8, lemma-fun, applied after choosing equal finite-rank coordinates; expands the last independence sentence in ILO VIII Lemma 3.2.12(ii), p.105.

proof.text: The map $\psi:\mathbf N^A\to R$, $(n_a)\mapsto\sum n_a a$, is onto by the stated generation hypothesis. If $\psi(n)=\psi(m)$, injectivity of $R\to G$ from [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] gives $\phi(n-m)=0$. Injectivity of $\phi$ in Step 7 yields $n=m$ coordinatewise. Thus $\psi$ is a bijective homomorphism, hence a monoid isomorphism (its inverse preserves addition by uniqueness of preimages). If $A$ is empty, generation forces $R=\{0\}$ and $G=0$, so $r=0$; $\mathbf N^{\varnothing}$ and $R$ are both the one-element monoid. All steps also allow $t=0$ and an arbitrary characteristic for $k$.

source.place: VIII, Lemma 3.2.12(ii), last sentence, p.105: the surjection from the free monoid is an isomorphism once the atoms are independent.

proof_origin.place: VIII Lemma 3.2.12(ii), pp.104--105: same dimension/cotangent/atom-independence route, with product-monoid and residue maps written explicitly and Stacks 00P0, 00KU and 05G8 supplying generic algebra tools.
